title: Ember Marketplace opportunity brief and outreach sketch
content:
Quick sketch / working notes for Ember Marketplace (EM) outreach.

Context and why this matters
- Ember is an SMB-focused e-commerce marketplace connecting ~4k merchants and 200 platform-integrated storefronts. They recently launched a storefront search beta and talked publicly about using embeddings/reranking.
- Opportunity: Embed Redwood as the inference engine powering a premium search + semantic recommendations offering (white-label) for higher GMV merchants. Two commercial hooks: revenue share on transactions & fixed monthly for Dedicated capacity for top-tier merchants.
- Why Redwood could win: predictable latency for storefront experiences (need < 60ms P95 for search), ability to run in a customer VPC/private deployment for larger merchants, and tooling to manage cost/quality tradeoffs across thousands of short queries.

Stakeholder map (initial guesses; need TO-confirm):
- Product lead: Priya Narayan (Head of Search & Recommendations) — owns roadmap for search beta
- Engineering: Platform infra lead — Mateo Alvarez (owner for partner integrations)
- Growth / Partnerships: Laila Owens — owns merchant partner programs and revenue-share pilots
- Top merchants (buyers): 3 merchants in pilot cohort — "Hearth & Found" (home), "Nimble Kids" (kids clothing), "Grove Gifts" (gifts)

Signals from public/partner pages (what I found)
- Ember dev blog Nov 2025: "experimenting with semantic ranking for query->product matches" (explicitly cites vector DB approach)
- Ember jobs: hiring "ML infra engineer - product search" — indicates productization phase
- Merchant forum: repeated complaints about search latency during sales events (peak load)

Technical fit notes / product asks we should be ready to answer
- Latency SLOs: Ember expects P95 < 60ms for search reranking in storefront path. Need to map to Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private (likely dedicated pools per region).
- Throughput profile: 10k QPS at peak across marketplace (est). Need autoscaling/burst story.
- Prefix caching / persistent KV cache: can cache merchant catalogs per shop to reduce repeated costs. Mention our automatic prefix caching and workload-aware batching.
- Data residency & security: some merchants (EU) will require KMS + audit logs. Highlight Redwood Private (VPC) and KMS/HSM integration.
- Edge routing: Ember has multi-region infra; show smart routing to run inference nearest to request.

Commercial considerations
- Pricing sensitivity: marketplace economics are tight — Ember likely prefers low per-query cost for standard search, and higher-priced premium for recommendation/LLM features.
- Pilot structure idea: 3-month pilot, fixed dedicated capacity for peak events + revenue share on upsell features (15% rev share for features using our scoring). For large merchants, optional private deployment at enterprise rates.

Primary objections we should prep for + rebuttals
1) Objection: "We already have a vector DB pipeline and a small reranker; we don't need a new vendor."
   Rebuttal: Redwood is complementary — can replace the reranker and provide predictable P95 latency and lower per-token costs via caching/batching. Offer 2-week PoC focused only on cold-start latency and a 1:1 comparison during peak load.
2) Objection: "Security/data residency — we can't send PII or merchant data to a hosted API."
   Rebuttal: Offer dedicated VPC/private deployment, KMS integration, and an audit log export. Share references (anonymized) for two customers in Europe who required the same.
3) Objection: "Cost predictability — per-token pricing is risky at scale."
   Rebuttal: Propose reserved capacity + autoscaling caps, and tooling from Redwood Optimize to recommend quantization/batching profiles to reduce unit costs. Provide an example costing model for a 10k daily queries merchant.
4) Objection: "Integration effort — we don't want to rip out our TF pipeline."
   Rebuttal: SDKs + streaming API can slot into existing pipelines. Offer an integration template with Ember's stack: short doc describing webhook/SDK integration (~3 day dev work) and a scoped SOW for our solutions engineering team.

Initial outreach cadence (6-touch sequence)
1) Email to Laila Owens (partnership): value intro + 1-pager attachment (pilot outline) — short, outcomes-oriented.
2) LinkedIn note to Priya Narayan: request 15-min intro focused on search beta.
3) Quick technical note to Mateo Alvarez with architecture sketch (how Redwood fits in their path) + ask for infra constraints.
4) Follow-up email with proposal for 2-week PoC + success criteria (latency, throughput, cost per query)
5) Offer calendar for a short technical deep-dive and a merchant demo for pilot cohort.
6) Final nudge with limited-time incentives (free dedicated capacity for first 30 days of pilot).

Sample cold email (working draft)
Subject: Fast, predictable semantic search for Ember storefronts — 2-week pilot idea
Hi Laila —
I saw Ember's search beta and love the direction. At Redwood Inference we help marketplaces run high-throughput, low-latency inference for search and recommendations (we power per-storefront reranking with P95 < 60ms in production).
If it helps, we'd be happy to run a focused 2-week PoC: integrate a single merchant from your beta (no model changes required), demonstrate latency and cost delta vs your current reranker, and provide a short proposal for a Dedicated capacity + pilot pricing model.
Quick Qs: who on your infra team should we loop in? Are there data residency constraints for merchants in your pilot?
Best,
Maya Chen

Call script / discovery bullets
- Confirm success metrics & owners (latency target, cost target, conversion uplift target)
- Current pipeline: vector DB used, where is reranking executed (client, search service, separate inference cluster)?
- Peak event behaviors: how many QPS spikes? retention window for prefix cache?
- Merchant segmentation: which merchants would pay for premium search?
- Security needs: audit log cadence, KMS, certifications required (SOC2, ISO27001)

Meeting agenda for pilot kickoff (if they accept)
- 5m intros and goals
- 10m technical architecture + integration plan (data flow mapping)
- 15m pilot plan: merchants, traffic split, monitoring & success criteria
- 10m ops: capacity, SLAs, security requirements
- 10m timeline & next steps (SOW, timeline to demo)

Success metrics to measure during pilot
- Latency: P95 end-to-end storefront reranking < 60ms
- Throughput: sustain X QPS with <10% degradation under peak (confirm actual target with Ember)
- Conversion: baseline vs pilot uplift on search -> add-to-cart (longer term)
- Cost: projected cost per 1k queries after caching/batching vs baseline cost

Admin / logistics notes
- Product collateral to attach: one-pager "Redwood for Marketplaces" (draft in /shared_drives/product/marketplaces/), Redwood SOC2 cert + KMS integration doc (linkable).
- Engineering contacts: loop Samir for architecture/benchmarks, Jules for pilot SOW/SE availability.
- Timeline preference: Ember is time-sensitive around next big sale (early Feb 2026) — propose pilot start Jan 20–30, finish before sale.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Get anonymized performance reference for a marketplace customer (ask Samir for a short 1-paragraph case study).
- Draft 1-pager tailored to merchant persona: search latency vs relevance uplift + cost table.
- Build quick Jupyter notebook comparing reranker latency with a small k-v cache sim (to show quick wins).
- Prep dedicated capacity pricing band for 1k, 5k, 10k QPS ranges.

Open questions to resolve before first outreach
- Confirm exact P95 target Ember expects (60ms is our assumption).
- Get list of pilot merchants and whether their catalogs are small (<10k SKUs) or large.
- Confirm GDPR/data residency constraints for EU merchants.

End of notes.

(Working doc: intentionally rough — keep iteration history here; move to shared_drives when we have an agreed pilot plan.)
